name: Permission modes
summary: The harness keeps allow, ask and deny rules per tool (and per command or path pattern) and switches between preset modes that change how much it asks. Rules are enforced by the harness, not by the model.
how: Write allow, ask and deny rules per tool or pattern, e.g. Bash(npm run *)
The harness checks each call: deny first, then ask, then allow
Pick a session mode (manual, accept edits, plan, auto, bypass) for everything the rules don't cover
Admins can pin or forbid modes through managed settings
facts: Claude Code, Codex (approval policies + sandbox modes)
default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions
Deny, then ask, then allow; first match wins (Claude Code)
Predictable, but rules drift and prompts cause approval fatigue
goodFor: Coding agents on a developer machine
Teams that check rules into the repo
watchOut: Broad allow rules quietly widen what the agent can do
Frequent prompts train people to click yes
